extracted.intended_audience: authors (women writers) considering submitting a manuscript to She Writes Press
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for submitting a book-length manuscript to She Writes Press, plus the publisher's editorial, production, distribution, and post-acceptance expectations. Covers what to submit, how submissions are evaluated (Green/Yellow/Red), proofreading/editing standards, production steps, distribution, and publicity notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission materials requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit the first 50 pages of your manuscript, along with a short synopsis, and chapter-by-chapter summaries. If you don’t have formal chapters, or you have a nonfiction book or outlier genre, approximate chapter summaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear chapter-by-chapter summaries; examples for fiction and memoir are linked. If your book lacks formal chapters, do your best to approximate. These materials are the basis for initial evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish-readiness assessed on merit of writing (not platform)
rubrics_metrics.description: She Writes Press only publishes manuscripts that they deem to be publish-ready, based purely on the merit of the writing and not on author platform or other subjective measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike self-publishing platforms, submissions are vetted for quality. The primary criterion is the writing itself rather than the author's platform, ensuring editorial standards similar to traditional publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: What readers evaluate: voice, style, structure, storytelling, cohesion
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are read for good writing, good storytelling, and cohesion; readers are looking for voice, style, and structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional readers (industry experts) will evaluate these qualities and provide a one-page evaluation that explains strengths and weaknesses. Strong voice, consistent style, coherent structure, and effective storytelling increase chances of a Green assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation timeline and track assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are a two-tiered process; within 6 weeks you will receive an assessment indicating your track: Green, Yellow, or Red.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The assessment is based on the first 50 pages and chapter summaries. This timeline gives authors an expectation for when editorial feedback and next steps will be delivered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Green Light (publish-ready) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Green track: authors whose work is deemed publish-ready will receive a Green assessment indicating readiness for publication and the level of editorial work required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Green assessment notes impressions based on the submitted materials and indicates any editorial work that is recommended or required. All Green manuscripts still receive final proofreading as part of the publishing package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yellow Light (contingent interest) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Yellow track: SWP is interested but has contingencies—e.g., manuscript needs trimming, a specific redirect, a sensitivity read, or consideration for a future season due to list capacity or overlapping subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The assessment will detail contingencies and suggest next steps for moving forward together. Yellow often implies revision is needed before formal acceptance; it may include scheduling considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Red Light (not a fit) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Red track: submissions carefully considered but not a right fit for SWP at this time. Writers are invited to resubmit in the future and may choose to work with a SWP-approved coach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Landing on Red does not preclude future consideration. Authors who work with approved coaches may resubmit with a waived submissions fee. Working with a coach does not guarantee a Green track or a contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission policy and submission-fee waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who work through a full revision with a SWP-approved coach are invited to resubmit directly and SWP will waive the submissions fee for resubmission. Authors who use an outside coach/editor may resubmit through Submittable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee waiver applies when engaging SWP-approved coaches. Resubmission is treated as a new submission; approved coaching increases support but does not guarantee acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading requirement (final manuscript)
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors publishing on She Writes Press will have their final manuscript proofread before going to layout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofreading is included in the publishing package to catch stylistic errors, typos, and grammatical mistakes. Manuscripts are reviewed by both a proofreader and the Project Manager to ensure quality control; SWP strives to publish error-free books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy-edit guidance and style guide
rubrics_metrics.description: If an assessment suggests a copy edit, SWP encourages but does not require using a She Writes Press copy editor. SWP copy editing is offered at $120/hour; their copy editors are proficient in the Chicago Manual of Style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can choose external copy editors or SWP editors. Chicago Manual of Style is the house style; copy editing may be recommended depending on the assessment but is not always mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover design standard and process
rubrics_metrics.description: She Writes Press includes a high-level custom cover design in the publishing package; cover design coincides with editing/proofreading and is treated as critically important to selling a book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors complete a cover memo to convey sensibilities and examples of appealing covers. SWP's Creative Director and team consult and direct the process to ensure competitiveness in the marketplace; they may offer title/subtitle support, back cover copy input, and leads to potential endorsers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interior layout & rounds after design
rubrics_metrics.description: Interior designers will create a custom layout once cover design is approved; authors will have opportunities to review and correct formatting mistakes, with typically two to three rounds of changes post-layout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Layout makes the manuscript look like a book and often reveals formatting issues; authors should expect to review and approve interior design and address small errors during these rounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final production steps and ARCs
rubrics_metrics.description: After finalizing cover and interior files, books are uploaded for POD or prepped for printing. Authors receive Advance Reader Copies (ARCs) as a last chance to catch errors. The cost of printing ARCs and final books is not included in the publishing package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SWP includes editorial review and edit of back cover copy as part of the package. Authors must review ARCs and submit any remaining final changes; SWP will update files and pass them to the printer and ebook converter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution model and channels
rubrics_metrics.description: SWP uses a hybrid model with traditional distribution through Simon & Schuster (S&S), placing books in trade distribution and Ingram's catalog (available via Edelweiss); S&S manages print and ebook distribution across 127 ebook partners and has international reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Traditional distribution provides visibility to big accounts, independent bookstores, libraries, online retailers, and specialty markets; SWP has a team of reps selling to the marketplace. While foreign bookstores can order efficiently, SWP does not maintain an active foreign sales force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicity responsibilities and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The She Writes Press publishing package does not include a dedicated publicity campaign. Most authors hire publicists; SWP provides a list of recommended publicists in the Author Handbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should plan for publicity costs and consider hiring a publicist; SWP supports authors with recommendations but does not run individualized publicity campaigns as part of the base package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing schedule and acquisition window
rubrics_metrics.description: SWP publishes books on seasonal lists and launches each season approximately 14–16 months prior to publication; at the time of this posting they are acquiring projects for Summer 2027 and cannot accommodate earlier publication dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be aware of seasonal scheduling and lead times; if an author needs to publish sooner than the available acquisition window, SWP cannot accommodate that timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted genres and subject areas
rubrics_metrics.description: SWP publishes a range of genres including Business/leadership, Women’s fiction, Genre fiction, Contemporary Fiction, Health/Fitness/Lifestyle, Literary Fiction, Memoir, Nonfiction, Self-help, Young adult (YA) fiction, Middle grade (MG) fiction, and Poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should confirm their manuscript fits one of the listed genres; outlier genres or nonfiction without chapters should provide approximate chapter summaries. Genre fit and seasonal list capacity can affect timing and acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author profit split and financial terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors invest in their publishing package up front and retain 60% of the net profits on print books and 70% of the net profits (minus a small distribution fee) on ebooks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This hybrid model combines author investment with traditional distribution advantages. Authors should understand upfront costs and the net-profit share structure as part of the publishing agreement.
